brief.topic: Why enterprises build an AI platform layer instead of many separate pilots
brief.audience: Enterprise AI leaders and platform PMs

coreInsight: A shared platform layer — access control, logging, evals and model routing — makes each new AI use case cheaper, but build it after a few real pilots, not before.

hooks.notes: Names a costly pattern enterprise teams recognise.

hooks.text: Your AI pilots are paying the same bill 50 times.
Why AI platforms beat AI pilots at scale.

selectionRationale: Highest total (22/25): the pattern is recognisable to the audience and the reel adds the honest trade-off on timing.

caption.opening: Every AI pilot needs the same plumbing: who can see what, what gets logged, how answers are checked, which model runs.
body:
Build that once as a shared layer and each new use case starts further ahead:
→ access control
→ logging and audit
→ evals and safety checks
→ model routing
The trade-off: a platform built before any pilot proves value tends to solve the wrong problems. Two or three real use cases first.

claims.text: A shared AI platform layer reduces the marginal cost of new use cases; building it after a few pilots reduces the risk of solving the wrong problems.
